abstract: Sullivan's celebrated no-wandering-domain theorem asserts that rational maps have no wandering Fatou components. In this paper, we establish a measure-theoretic counterpart for the Julia set: every wandering continuum in the Julia set of a finite-type entire function has zero area. For infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials, we also prove that almost every point in the renormalization core (the intersection of the orbits of little Julia sets) is recurrent and contained in the postcritical set. The main tool is a conservativity theorem: if $f$ is injective on a forward invariant measurable subset $E$ of the Julia set, then $f|_E$ is conservative and almost every point of $E$ is recurrent and contained in the postsingular set.
hook: Wandering continua in Julia sets of finite-type entire functions have zero area
summary: Sullivan's theorem rules out wandering regions in the Fatou set; this paper gives a counterpart for the Julia set. It proves that wandering continua in the Julia set of a finite-type entire function have zero area, via a conservativity theorem. The result concerns area only and says nothing about whether such continua exist.
title: Wandering continua, renormalization, and Lebesgue measure on Julia sets
